I will keep my land in the usual Quzhou pattern: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same field. That is the crop path I trust most here. In Quzhou, wheat and maize are still the main crops, and local production is built around that system, with surface-water spring irrigation for wheat and high seed coverage for the main grains ([农业农村部](https://www.moa.gov.cn/xw/qg/202107/t20210720_6372348.htm), [邯郸日报转载](https://finance.sina.cn/2025-02-25/detail-inemsnhi1331852.d.html?cid=76729&node_id=76729&oid=%E5%AE%9D%E7%8F%80%E5%A5%B3%E8%A1%A8%E5%AE%98%E6%96%B9%E4%BB%B7%E6%A0%BC%E2%86%92%E5%BE%AE%E4%BF%A189486682%E2%86%92lizF&vt=4)). I am 67, so I will choose the simpler, more mechanized, lower-risk route instead of chasing cotton or vegetables. I do not want a crop that needs constant picking, more hiring, or more market gambling.

I will manage for steady income and solid yield, not for the highest possible output. For wheat, I will use improved seed, deep plough after maize straw return, put on moderate fertilizer, and give two irrigations because wheat here usually needs the water more than maize. For maize, I will sow right after wheat harvest with no-tillage seeding, use hybrid seed, keep fertilizer slightly lower than wheat, and usually irrigate once because summer rain does most of the work. I will keep pesticide use controlled: enough to protect the crop, not the old heavy way. My yield target is below the best demonstration fields in Quzhou, but close enough to be realistic for a careful older farmer farming in a familiar way ([中国农大曲周实验站](https://qzsyz.cau.edu.cn/art/2024/10/8/art_46317_1039835.html), [农业农村部冬小麦施肥指导](https://www.moa.gov.cn/xw/zxfb/202209/t20220922_6411293.htm)).
